definition: An Aramaic word meaning Father, used by Jesus in prayer and by believers addressing God with trust.
God's welcome of believers into his family, giving them the standing and inheritance of his children.
A place where offerings or sacrifices are presented to God; biblical altars also mark worship and encounters with him.
A Hebrew expression of affirmation meaning truly or so be it, used to confirm a statement or prayer.
A heavenly messenger or servant of God. The underlying biblical words can also describe human messengers, depending on context.
Applying oil to set someone apart for a role or to signify blessing; Scripture also speaks of anointing by the Holy Spirit.
A revelation or unveiling. Apocalyptic writing uses visions and symbols to disclose God's judgment, victory, and hope.
One who is sent with a commission, especially the witnesses commissioned by Jesus to proclaim the gospel.
The sacred chest associated with God's covenant with Israel, containing the testimony and standing in the sanctuary.
The risen Jesus being taken up into heaven, where Christians confess that he reigns with the Father.
The restoration of relationship with God through dealing with sin. Christians understand Jesus' self-offering as central to this reconciliation.
The Christian rite involving water, associated with repentance, forgiveness, and union with Christ. Traditions differ on its administration and explanation.
Jesus' declarations of blessing that introduce the Sermon on the Mount; a related series appears in Luke.
Speech or conduct that dishonors God or treats what is holy with contempt. Biblical accusations must be read in their particular context.
Spiritual birth from above through God's Spirit, described by Jesus in his conversation with Nicodemus.
The collection of books a religious community recognizes as Scripture. Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant Old Testament collections differ.
The Greek title meaning Anointed One, corresponding to Messiah; it identifies Jesus' calling rather than a family name.
The community of those called together in Christ, whether a local assembly or the whole body of believers.
The bodily sign of God's covenant with Abraham; Scripture also uses circumcision of the heart for inward faithfulness.
An instruction expressing God's will for human life, including love of God and neighbor.
Open acknowledgment, either of sin before God or of faith in him, according to the context.
A binding relationship established through promises and obligations. Biblical covenants shape the story of God's dealings with his people.
God's bringing the world and living creatures into existence and ordering them as good.
Execution on a cross, the form of death Jesus suffered under Roman authority; central to the Christian proclamation of salvation.
A biblical expression for God's decisive intervention in judgment and deliverance; its setting and emphasis vary by passage.
A servant or minister in the Christian community, associated with practical service and recognized church responsibilities.
Old Testament books received as canonical in Catholic tradition but placed outside the Old Testament canon by most Protestants. Orthodox collections vary; terminology also differs.
A learner and follower. Jesus calls disciples to follow his teaching and pattern of life.
A letter, especially one of the New Testament writings addressed to churches or individuals for instruction and encouragement.
Life in communion with God through Jesus Christ, beginning in the present and reaching fulfillment beyond death.
Meaning thanksgiving; a Christian name for the Lord's Supper, instituted by Jesus with bread and wine. Traditions differ in explaining Christ's presence and the rite.
Sharing the good news of Jesus Christ and inviting others to respond in faith.
Removal from one's homeland, especially Israel's and Judah's deportations under foreign powers. Exile and return shape many biblical promises.
Israel's departure from slavery in Egypt under Moses; also the name of the biblical book recounting that deliverance and the covenant at Sinai.
Trust in God and a response to his faithfulness, expressed in belief and lived allegiance.
Voluntarily abstaining from food for a time as part of prayer, repentance, mourning, or seeking God.
The release of sin or wrongdoing from being held against someone; Scripture calls people to receive God's mercy and forgive others.
A person from the nations other than Israel; in many New Testament contexts, someone who is not Jewish.
The splendor, honor, and revealed greatness of God; the word can also describe honor given or received.
Good news, especially the proclamation of God's saving work in Jesus Christ; also one of the four New Testament accounts of his life and ministry.
God's freely given favor and help, through which he calls, forgives, and transforms people.
A Hebrew expression meaning praise the Lord, used as an invitation or acclamation of worship.
Being set apart for God and reflecting his goodness. God's holiness expresses his incomparable purity and majesty.
The Spirit of God, confessed in Christianity as the third person of the Trinity, who gives life, guides, and strengthens believers.
Confident expectation rooted in God's faithfulness, especially his promises of resurrection and the renewal of creation.
Giving worship or ultimate allegiance to a created thing in place of God.
The Christian belief that the eternal Word became human in Jesus Christ, truly sharing human life.
Prayer offered on behalf of others; Scripture also describes Christ's intercession for believers.
Being put right with God through his grace. Christian traditions differ in explaining its relationship to faith, works, and sanctification.
God's sovereign reign, made known in Jesus and awaited in its fullness; more than a geographic territory.
A title for Jesus connecting his saving work with biblical imagery of sacrificial lambs and deliverance.
An honest expression of grief, protest, or distress brought before God, often joined with trust or a plea for help.
Torah means instruction. It can refer to God's teaching, the law given through Moses, or the first five books of Scripture.
Compassion shown to those in need or guilt, expressed through help, forgiveness, and faithful love.
The Hebrew-derived title meaning Anointed One, associated with God's promised deliverer; Christians identify Jesus as the Messiah.
An extraordinary act understood as a sign of God's power and purpose, such as healing or deliverance.
A story or comparison that invites reflection on God's kingdom, human conduct, or spiritual truth.
The Jewish festival recalling God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt; the New Testament also connects Passover imagery with Christ.
The fiftieth-day festival associated with the Jewish Feast of Weeks; Acts recounts the Holy Spirit's coming upon Jesus' followers at Pentecost.
A member of a Jewish movement concerned with faithful observance and interpretation of the law. The Gospels portray diverse encounters with Pharisees, not a single uniform response.
Turning to God in praise, thanksgiving, confession, petition, or attentive trust.
A message communicated on God's behalf, calling people to faithfulness and sometimes announcing future events.
The restoration of a broken relationship, especially the peace with God made possible through Christ.
Deliverance pictured as release from bondage or the payment of a ransom; in Christianity, freedom from sin through Christ.
Turning away from sin and toward God, involving a changed heart and a changed direction of life.
God's raising of the dead, centrally Jesus' rising and the promised future raising of the dead.
The seventh day set apart for rest and worship in Israel's covenant life, recalling creation and deliverance.
God's deliverance from sin, evil, and death, bringing people into restored life with him.
Being made holy or set apart for God; also the ongoing transformation of believers by God's grace.
Thought, action, or failure to act that violates God's will and damages relationship with God and neighbor.
The Christian confession of one God in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The term summarizes teaching drawn from Scripture rather than appearing as a biblical word.
Honoring God through praise, prayer, obedience, and the offering of one's life to him.
